paths.description: Homepage/news portal: primary discovery surface and global chrome, consent, privacy, performance and responsive behavior.
Tin tức trong ngày listing: representative section/index template. Represents other editorial category listings.
Lead article: representative detail/reading journey, metadata, no-JS content and mobile layout.

Search, social network /mxh, video playback, account and ad conversion flows were not covered because they are distinct products or require deeper interaction beyond the representative public news-reading task.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: white content and consent surfaces remain unchanged under prefers-color-scheme: dark.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border and control tokens.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, found no matching CSS rule, and still found two running 700 ms animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce rule that removes non-essential animation and auto-advance.

findings.summary: Primary page changes are abrupt and do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero view-transition rules across the rendered homepage styles; navigation is a conventional full-document swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same- or cross-document View Transitions for primary article and section navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long news pages provide static rather than scroll-state-aware navigation.
findings.evidence: The homepage/article screenshots show fixed dense chrome and floating controls, while CSS inspection found no container scroll-state or declarative scroll timeline support.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state-aware sticky chrome or a lightweight reading-progress affordance while preserving content space.

findings.summary: The consent interstitial blocks all content and breaks at the mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: Every entry capture shows a full-page consent interruption. At 360×800, its fixed 512 px panel is mostly off-screen to the right and the consent/refusal controls are not visible in the initial viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a responsive semantic dialog with max-inline-size: calc(100vw - 2rem), visible equal-weight accept/refuse actions, focus containment and reliable dismissal.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is not exposed as a native dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection reported zero dialog and popover elements while the screenshots show a modal overlay that blocks the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the blocking consent flow with <dialog> and its native focus/top-layer behavior, retaining accessible buttons and light dismissal only where lawful.

findings.summary: Dense navigation, floating controls, social modules and consent chrome compete with the news content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and article screenshots devote substantial space to two navigation rows, floating home/up buttons and a full overlay before the article can be read.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent chrome, defer non-primary modules, and keep the article and lead stories visually dominant.

findings.summary: The desktop layout is forced into the mobile viewport.
findings.evidence: At 360×800 the layout primitive measured scrollWidth 1080 against clientWidth 360, 720 px horizontal overflow. The screenshot shows the page and consent controls clipped off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed desktop widths/device branching, honor the device-width viewport, and build fluid layouts that fit 320–400 px without horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Reusable story and navigation components do not adapt to their containers.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero container queries, while the narrow capture retained a 1080 px desktop composition and clipped cards/overlay.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and navigation components containment and size-aware container-query layouts, with fluid intrinsic fallbacks.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and target sizing are insufficient.
findings.evidence: The focused first link computed to outline-style none, Lighthouse failed target-size, and the probe found a 130×16 input plus many zero-sized hidden controls in the active consent DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Use :focus-visible with a clear high-contrast outline and ensure active touch targets are at least 44×44 CSS px with spacing.

findings.summary: Reading a story is blocked on mobile by an unreachable consent decision.
findings.evidence: The homepage, section and article all open behind consent; at 360 px the decision buttons are outside the initial visible panel because the overlay is clipped.
findings.suggestedFix: Make reject/accept controls immediately reachable at every supported viewport and persist the choice before loading optional trackers.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 18.3 s (performance 0.61); the trace independently measured LCP at 4.02 s under a different desktop run, still above the 2.5 s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the lead image/content, remove consent/ad work from the critical path, and defer non-critical scripts and below-fold modules.

findings.summary: The initial page has a heavy, third-party-dominated dependency graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 143 requests and 4,437,907 transferred bytes; 140 requests and 4,340,098 bytes were classified third-party, including parser-inserted advertising scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Shorten the critical chain, self-host/trim essentials, defer ad auctions and optional modules, compress scripts, and apply effective cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused and legacy JavaScript are shipped.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 949 KiB of unused JavaScript and 48 KiB of legacy JavaScript; HAR shows 1.47 MB transferred script bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by feature, conditionally load ad/social modules, remove legacy duplication, and ship a modern bundle.

findings.summary: Main-thread work is excessive even though measured blocking bursts were modest.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 3.2 s main-thread work and 190 ms TBT; the separate trace had no >50 ms tasks, indicating cumulative scripting rather than one isolated stall.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile script evaluation and split or schedule non-critical work by priority; delay auctions/social widgets until needed.

findings.summary: Many links and images have no usable accessible name.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 42 images without alt text; the DOM probe found 47 anchors with no text, aria-label, or named image; Lighthouse failed image-alt and link-name.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt text or empty alt for decorative images and ensure every actionable link has a discernible name.

findings.summary: Text fails minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s color-contrast audit failed on the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text and control color tokens to meet WCAG AA in all normal, dark and high-contrast states.

findings.summary: Heading structure and keyboard focus are not reliable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the DOM contains empty H1/H2 nodes from the consent UI and the focused first link had outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove empty headings, preserve a sequential document outline, and apply a visible :focus-visible indicator in reading order.

findings.summary: Viewport scaling and reflow do not provide an inclusive narrow-screen experience.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport and target-size; the viewport specifies maximum-scale=1.0, and the mobile layout overflows by 720 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale restrictions, support user zoom, reflow at narrow widths, and enlarge undersized targets.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the errors-in-console audit on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the recorded network/runtime errors and add production monitoring that prevents recurring uncaught failures.

findings.summary: Image markup is structurally weak and wastes bytes.
findings.evidence: Although doctype and UTF-8 are valid, 99 of 100 inspected images lacked explicit dimensions and 43 were oversized for display.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, and correctly sized modern image variants.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and DevTools inspector issues remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated API warning and failed inspector-issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace deprecated API use and clear DevTools Issues, especially cookie and browser-policy warnings.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable or descriptively named.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors; DOM recon found a javascript:void(0) anchor and 47 unnamed anchors. The mobile viewport is also not usable despite a viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations or buttons for actions, add descriptive accessible link names, and fix mobile reflow.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but security headers and cookie attributes are unsafe.
findings.evidence: Headers found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. All eight observed first-party cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None; several analytics/consent cookies last 390–400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a nonce/hash CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark HTTPS cookies Secure and use the least-permissive SameSite/lifetime.

findings.summary: The page exposes users to an unusually broad advertising/tracking surface.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 39 third-party origins and 12 known tracker domains. HAR classified 140 of 143 requests and 4.34 MB as third-party-origin traffic.
findings.suggestedFix: Block optional third parties until valid consent, reduce vendors, proxy/self-host essentials, batch analytics, and document retention and purpose.

findings.summary: The blocking consent runtime is not resilient at narrow viewports.
findings.evidence: The same consent component remains fixed-width and clipped on homepage and article at 360×800, placing recovery/decision controls outside the visible region.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the dialog intrinsically responsive, scroll its internal content, pin decision controls within its visible block, and test 320 px/zoom conditions.

findings.summary: Images are broadly unoptimised for their display contexts.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 43 were oversized, 75 lacked srcset, 42 used legacy formats and 93 below-fold images were not marked lazy.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants, use srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold media, and avoid full-resolution thumbnails.

findings.summary: Advertising and third-party media dominate the page budget.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 4.44 MB across 143 requests, with 4.34 MB classified third-party; scripts alone were 1.47 MB and images 2.70 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template byte/request budgets, delay third-party auctions until consent/visibility, and remove vendors or media that do not justify their cost.
